Visit note | 2025-04-20 03:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Harun Shikder, 72, male. Mr. Shikder attends today because a routine health check revealed high cholesterol levels, though he currently has no physical symptoms. He works as a homemaker, and this finding was discovered after a relative's heart attack in Shyamoli prompted him to get tested. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies chest discomfort, breathlessness, dizziness, or palpitations. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.5 mmol/L, BP 111/79 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 84 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds, and his lungs are clear to auscultation. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: referral to Endocrinology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up after the Endocrinology review.
